html:
SMTO-GML-0006 — SMTO couldn't read your attached file correctly

GUID: 8237bd18-67ce-488b-b09c-e7064dc44b75
Slug: gmail-attachment-unavailable
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO started reading a file you attached to the conversation, but it couldn't read all of it, or what it read didn't match the file you uploaded. SMTO didn't send the email so a broken file wouldn't go out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Add context under the message box, choose Add files to conversation, and attach the same file again from your computer. A fresh upload gives SMTO a complete copy it can check.
  2. Ask SMTO to send or draft the email again using the file you just attached. SMTO must use the new copy, not the one that failed the check.
  3. If it fails again, open the file on your computer to make sure it opens normally, then attach it once more. A damaged or still-changing file can't be read the same way twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the email or draft with the file attached, and the file opens correctly for the person who receives it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's saved data or files to get past this; the check is there to stop a broken file being sent.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Outgoing Gmail attachment read from conversation Context failed: a chunked read did not advance its offset, or the assembled bytes did not match the SHA-256 recorded when the file was uploaded.

What this means

  • Outgoing upload reading fails to advance its offset or assembled bytes do not match the stored context SHA-256. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Outgoing upload reading fails to advance its offset or assembled bytes do not match the stored context SHA-256.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original upload's read progress and digest without replacing it with preview text.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the Context item for this conversation in the Server log and artifact storage: the stored bytes are incomplete or no longer match the recorded sha256. Have the user upload the file again as a new Context item and reference that; do not bypass the hash check or delete stored state to make the read succeed.
  • Restore the required task artifact context or refresh the live message attachment.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact granted attachment bytes are read completely and match their retained hash.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
